summary: Claude Code loaded the requesting-code-review skill, dispatched a reviewer subagent, and returned a precise review: both real bugs (SQL injection, plaintext password ===) flagged as Critical, verdict "Ready to merge? No", and no Critical/Important findings against any of the six clean items.
reasoning: The full flow completed as the story describes: single prompt, skill loaded, Agent subagent dispatched with the reviewer template, and a structured review returned. Both planted bugs were caught as Critical, merge was refused, and the six correct hunks drew nothing above Minor. The only non-blocking oddity is the 'hyperpowers:' vs 'superpowers:' plugin namespace, which I recorded as an observation rather than a criterion failure since it is the same skill file and the subagent path was exercised.

observations.description: Skill namespace mismatch with the user's request: the user asked for 'superpowers:requesting-code-review' and the agent invoked 'hyperpowers:requesting-code-review' without comment. Same skill content, but the rename is silent and could confuse a spec-aware user.

The main agent waited for the backgrounded subagent using literal `sleep 60` then `sleep 90` bash calls ('Waiting for reviewer subagent · 1m 2s'). Polling via blocking sleeps is wasteful and inflates wall-clock time.

The review included a self-promotional install blurb: 'codex-plugin-cc is not available ... Install it for an extra gate: /plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc ...' — noise in a code review deliverable.

Reviewer Minor #5 claims displayName returns undefined for {user:{}} and suggests optional chaining; this is arguably out-of-scope speculation about a case the guard was not written for, though correctly ranked Minor.
Reviewer mentions 'I recorded the ungated range in the review ledger' — an internal bookkeeping detail surfaced to the user without explanation of what the ledger is or where it lives.

criteria.criterion: Skill superpowers:requesting-code-review loaded and Agent subagent dispatched
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use entries: {"name":"Skill","inp":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review\"}"} and {"name":"Agent","inp":"{\"subagent_type\":\"general-purpose\",\"description\":\"Review code changes\"...}"} in b7e31710-...jsonl; subagent log file agent-a18e395ad9a1a49c8.jsonl created. Note: the plugin namespace rendered as 'hyperpowers:' not 'superpowers:' (same skill path .../skills/requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md).

criteria.criterion: SQL injection in findUserByEmail flagged Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent report: "#### Critical (Must Fix) **1. SQL injection: the parameterized query was replaced with string concatenation — src/db.js:6-10**" with the concatenated query quoted.

criteria.criterion: Plaintext password comparison in login flagged Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent report: "**2. Password verification downgraded to plaintext equality — src/db.js:15** ... if (user && user.password === password) ... Even granting plaintext storage, `===` is not timing-safe" — listed under Critical (Must Fix).

criteria.criterion: Reviewer did NOT approve the diff for merge
criteria.evidence: Subagent: "**Ready to merge?** No"; main agent screen: "Recommendation: do not merge as-is."

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding against the six correct items
criteria.evidence: Only two Critical (db.js SQL injection, plaintext password) and two Important (#3 removed email validation guard in src/db.js:5 — part of the diff's db.js rewrite, not one of the six; #4 no tests for findUserByEmail/login). expiresAt/86400 and displayName appear only as Minor (#6, #5); test fixture apiKey only as Minor #7; toMinutes drew no finding (grep of the review text shows no 'toMinutes' mention); close()/void and describe() were praised: "the `void` on `recordLatency` correctly matches the documented fire-and-forget contract", "describe() covers the full state vocabulary with an explicit default".

criteria.criterion: Minor/Nice-to-have on those six do not fail
criteria.evidence: The three touching clean items (expiresAt magic number/validation, displayName fallback, unused apiKey fixture) were all filed under "#### Minor (Nice to Have)" — permitted by this criterion.
